title: Segmented security-response micro-packs and credit-triggering experiment
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build and validate a packaging experiment that delivers small, composable SIG/CAIQ response micro-packs ("segmented response sets") mapped to customer risk tiers and tied to automatic crediting rules. The goal is to reduce time-to-response for common questionnaire asks, reduce manual SE effort, and create a measurable self-serve path that converts into paid entitlements for enterprise customers that need full attestation bundles.
background: Sales and Solutions Engineering spend ~40% of questionnaire cycles assembling bespoke answers for mid-market customers. Current large attestation bundles are costly to produce and create friction. Recent pilots indicate customers frequently request ~7-12 canonical answers repeatedly across deals. We want to productize those frequently-requested slices into reusable micro-packs and evaluate whether offering them as low-friction add-ons or credit-conditioned unlocks reduces cycle time and increases paid conversions.
goals: Decrease SE/manual response time per questionnaire by 50% for mid-market deals
Establish 3 micro-pack bundles covering 80% of repeat questions observed in last 6 months
Measure revenue impact: +5% attach rate for security-pack add-on in pilot cohorts
Create a reproducible credit-triggering rule so sales can grant micro-packs without legal intervention
success_metrics: Median time from customer request to delivered response set (target: <=48 hours)
Number of deals using micro-packs (target: 30 pilot deals in Q2)
Reduction in SE hours spent preparing responses (target: -40% for pilot cohort)
Attach-to-contract conversion delta vs baseline (target: +5 percentage points)
proposed_solution: 1) Analyze questionnaire logs to identify high-frequency questions and theme clusters. 2) Author 3 candidate micro-packs (Compliance Basics, Network & Encryption Snapshot, Data Residency Summary) with templated language and evidentiary links. 3) Build console flow and sales UI to select/grant micro-packs; grant can be free credit (one-off) or attached as paid add-on depending on deal size. 4) Instrument metrics and billing events; add simple audit trail entries for granted packs.
acceptance_criteria: Three micro-packs authored and approved by Security and Legal
Console/MX flow allows selection and grant of a micro-pack with an audit log entry
Pilot cohort of at least 20 customer requests processed through micro-packs
Dashboard displays time-to-delivery, usage, and attach/conversion metrics for pilot
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: data analysis and pack definitions. Week 3-4: content authoring + Security/Legal review. Week 5: implement grant UI and crediting rule in console (feature flag). Week 6-8: pilot with Sales + 20 customers and collect metrics. Week 9: evaluate results and decide on scaling or iterate.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Legal/security rejects templated language -> Mitigation: route to Security for pre-approval and include conservative wording and pointers to evidentiary artifacts
Risk: Customers view micro-packs as insufficient -> Mitigation: offer easy escalation path to full attestation with SLA and clear pricing transparency
Risk: Billing complexity with one-off credits -> Mitigation: partner with Finance to model credit accounting and keep initial pilot credit-offers limited and manually reconciled

next_steps: Confirm Security/Legal approval on candidate language (owner: Priya). Scope UI work with Eng (ENG-12091) and get design mockups for console grant flow. Schedule pilot cohort with Sales Ops and prepare measurement dashboard with Analytics.
customer_communication: Draft two email templates: (1) micro-pack offer explaining scope and how to escalate; (2) follow-up request for additional attestation (if needed). Ensure marketing language is approved by Legal.
notes_for_reviewers: When reviewing, focus on: 1) completeness of evidence links for each pack, 2) legal risk in templated wording, 3) operational friction in granting credits. Prefer conservative language at pilot phase.
